answer.worked:
Subtract $3m$ from both sides, then subtract $2$ and divide by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}7&=5m+2\\5&=5m\\1&=m\end{align*}$$

Subtract $4t$ from both sides, then add $6$ and divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}3t-6&=5\\3t&=11\\t&=\frac{11}{3}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $2h$ from both sides, then add $8$ and divide by $4$.
$$\begin{align*}4h-8&=-7\\4h&=1\\h&=\frac{1}{4}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $3w$ from both sides, then add $4$ and divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}12&=3w-4\\16&=3w\\\frac{16}{3}&=w\end{align*}$$

Subtract $2p$ from both sides, then divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}3p&=8\\p&=\frac{8}{3}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $2p$ from both sides, then divide by $3$.
$$\begin{align*}3p&=-8\\p&=-\frac{8}{3}\end{align*}$$

Subtract $k$ from both sides, then add $3$ and divide by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}-19&=5k-3\\-16&=5k\\-\frac{16}{5}&=k\end{align*}$$

Collect like terms on the right. Subtract $t$ from both sides, then divide by $5$.
$$\begin{align*}6t&=t+8\\5t&=8\\t&=\frac{8}{5}\end{align*}$$

Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-3d6070fd08]
Finding: The topic has no opening review of collecting like terms with signed coefficients and solving two-step equations, both used directly in its introductory demonstrations.

The identify demonstrations use coefficient collection; the right-hand worked example requires solving 7=3x+1. Proposed repair (add-review): Before reuse-s5-p80-information-block, add: '1 Simplify: 7x-3x. 2 Simplify: -2x+5x. 3 Solve: 3x+1=7. 4 Solve: 3-2x=9.' Answers: 4x; 3x; x=2; x=-3. Keep the review within one page.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-d59e53626d]
Idea: Extend the existing equation comparison by changing both constants equally, then changing only one.
Why: The follow-up exposes why adding the same amount to both sides preserves the solution, whereas changing only one side changes it.
Proposed addition: After reuse-s5-p86-q9-reflection, add: (d) 'Increase both constants in 5x+12=3x+16 by 5. Solve the new equation.' Answer: 5x+17=3x+21, x=2. (e) 'Instead, increase only the left constant in the original equation by 5. Solve the new equation.' Answer: 5x+17=3x+16, x=-1/2. (f) 'Why did the solution stay the same in part d?' Answer: adding 5 to both sides preserves equality for the original solution.
